in_text_mentions: l intake for the last 24 hours. Blood work, electrocardiogram, and chest X-ray were unremarkable. The patient was admitted to hospital for further workup. Upon admission to hospital, a CT scan of the chest and abdomen showed thickening of the distal esophagus (Figure 1). Esophagogastroduodenoscopy was performed the following day and revealed ulcerative esophagitis at the mid-esophagus at 15 cm and at the gastroesophageal junction at 40 cm (Figures 2, 3, and 4). The findings on endoscopy were most consistent with pill esophagitis. The findings were not typical of CMV, HSV, or candida infection.
